body:
OBSERVED FLAKY 2026-08-19, with both directions measured before blaming anything.

THE FAILURE. Full suite on branch `adlc-1.10-upgrade`:

    FAIL test/gateway/listing-warm.test.ts > a bulk of 5k plain arrivals folds in one read
    Error: Test timed out in 60000ms.  (listing-warm.test.ts:147)
    Test Files 1 failed | 232 passed    Tests 1 failed | 2267 passed

MEASURED BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what makes this attributable:
- ISOLATION, same branch: PASSES, 28.58s for 16 tests.
- FULL SUITE on main, same machine: PASSES, 51.97s.
- FULL SUITE on the branch, second run: PASSES, 51.76s.
- The test imports NOTHING from src/server. The branch's only source change was
  src/server/http.ts (the listen path). The diff cannot reach this test.

So it is load-sensitive, not diff-caused and not broken: ~28s of work under a 60s per-test override,
which the suite's parallel load can exceed. The margin looks like 2x and is not, because the
denominator moves with whatever else is running.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. Every gate in this repo reads an exit code as a verdict: P5
evidence binds a revision, a self-merge hangs on a green bar, hollow-test refuses a non-green
baseline outright. A test that is sometimes red makes each of those a coin flip, and trains whoever
sees red to re-run instead of investigate.

THE RAIL IS FROZEN. It is T163's declared rail and T163 is archived, so the CI backstop guards it.
Fixing it is an authorized edit, which is why this is a ticket rather than a repair.

DIAGNOSE BEFORE FIXING — it is a RAIL bug, not a spec-accuracy bug. The promise (a bulk folds in one
read, no scan) is TRUE; what is load-dependent is the fixture's runtime, not the assertion's force.

DO NOT fix it by widening the timeout. That converts a visible flake into a hidden performance
regression: the rail's whole point is that folding does not scale with the ground, and a bigger
budget is exactly how a scan-shaped regression would slip through green. Prefer a fixture whose cost
does not ride wall-clock — assert the scan count (already spied) at a bulk size chosen for
detectability rather than for drama, and if the large bulk earns its keep as a performance probe,
give it its own file so a slow machine cannot take the correctness rail down with it.

TWO-SIDED, as ever: the fix must still FAIL if the fold starts scanning. A rail that stops being
flaky by stopping being sensitive has been deleted, not repaired.
title: The 5k bulk-fold rail times out under suite load — a frozen rail that is sometimes red
